blocks.content: Light is a form of energy that enables us to see objects. It is a type of electromagnetic radiation that travels in straight lines. Light plays an important role in vision, optical instruments and many natural phenomena.
1. Nature of Light

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Light travels in a straight line in a homogeneous transparent medium, known as rectilinear propagation.
Reflection of light obeys two main laws: the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie on the same plane, and the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Refraction occurs when light passes from one transparent medium to another, changing speed and bending towards or away from the normal.
Convex lenses converge light rays to form real or virtual images, while concave lenses diverge light rays to form virtual, erect, and diminished images.
Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component seven spectrum colors (VIBGYOR) when passing through a glass prism.

blocks.content: • Light is a form of energy.
• It travels in straight lines.
• Light does not require a material medium for propagation.
• The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 3 × 10^8 m/s.
2. Sources of Light
3. Reflection of Light
Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it strikes a surface.
Laws of Reflection:
• Angle of incidence = Angle of reflection.
Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation that enables the human eye to perceive objects.
• Incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
4. Types of Reflection
5. Refraction of Light
Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another.
Examples:

rows: Bouncing back of light rays into the same medium upon striking a surface
Bending of light rays when passing obliquely from one medium to another
Occurs within a single optical medium
Requires two media of different optical densities
Remains constant as the medium does not change
Changes depending on the refractive index of the new medium
Angle of incidence (i) = Angle of reflection (r)
Snell's Law: sin(i) / sin(r) = constant (Refractive Index)

blocks.content: • A pencil appears bent in water.
• Mirage in deserts.

7. Optical Instruments
• Microscope – used to see small objects.
• Telescope – used to observe distant objects.

8. Dispersion of Light

items: Snell's Law (n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2) is frequently tested in numerical problems regarding refraction across media.
Myopia (nearsightedness) is corrected using concave lenses, whereas Hypermetropia (farsightedness) requires convex lenses.
Total Internal Reflection occurs only when light moves from a denser to a rarer medium at an incident angle greater than the critical angle.

blocks.content: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component colors when it passes through a prism. The seven colors are Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red.
Important Facts
• Speed of light is approximately 3 × 10^8 m/s.
• Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
• Convex lens converges light rays.
• Dispersion of light produces seven colors.
